title: Set 192

sentences.ko: 원래 뒷마당에서 파티하기로 했는데, 세 시 넘어서 천둥번개 온다고 하더라. 그래서 아무래도 다들 거실에 몰아넣어야 할 것 같아.
sentences.text: We were supposed to have the party out in the backyard, but they're saying thunderstorms after three, so I guess we're cramming everybody into the living room.

alts.text: Party was gonna be out back, but they're calling for storms after three, so looks like everybody's getting squeezed into the living room.
We had planned to hold the party in the backyard, but thunderstorms are forecast after three o'clock, so I suppose we will have to fit everyone into the living room.

sentences.note: **cramming** 은 좁은 곳에 억지로 꽉 채워 넣는다는 말이에요. **they're saying** 은 일기예보나 소문처럼 누가 말하는지 딱 정하지 않고 그렇다더라 할 때 써요.

sentences.ko: 너는 맨날 뭘 보든 상관없다고 해놓고, 내가 뭘 고르기만 하면 바로 음, 그건 별로, 이러잖아. 그러니까 그냥 보고 싶은 거 말해!
sentences.text: You always say you don't care what we watch, and then the second I pick something, you're like, eh, not that one. So just tell me what you want!

alts.text: Every time it's, oh, I don't care what we watch, and then the minute I pick something you go, eh, not that one. Just tell me what you want!
You always say that you do not mind what we watch, yet as soon as I choose something, you say you would rather not watch that one. Please simply tell me what you would like!

sentences.note: **the second I** 는 내가 ~하자마자 라는 뜻이에요. **you're like** 는 말이나 반응을 흉내 낼 때 쓰는 아주 흔한 구어예요.

sentences.ko: 걔 친해지면 진짜 웃긴데, 처음엔 좀 조용한 편이야. 그러니까 처음 10분 동안 말을 거의 안 해도 너무 신경 쓰지 마.
sentences.text: She's really funny once she warms up, but she's kind of quiet at first, so don't take it personally if she barely says anything for the first ten minutes.

alts.text: Once she warms up she's super funny, but she's kinda quiet at first, so don't take it personally if she hardly talks the first ten minutes.
She is very amusing once she becomes comfortable, but she tends to be rather quiet at first, so please do not take it personally if she says very little during the first ten minutes.

sentences.note: **warms up** 은 사람이 낯을 풀고 편해진다는 뜻이에요. **don't take it personally** 는 너 때문이 아니니 마음에 담아 두지 말라는 말이에요.
sentences.situation: 친구 소개팅 주선하면서 상대가 어떤 사람인지 설명하기

sentences.ko: 연말까지만 버티자고 계속 스스로 다짐하는데, 일요일 밤만 되면 속이 조여드는 것 같아. 좋아하는 일이면 이런 기분이 들면 안 되는 거 아닌가 싶어.
sentences.text: I keep telling myself I'll stay until the end of the year, but every Sunday night I get this knot in my stomach, and I don't think you're supposed to feel like that about a job you like.

alts.text: I'm gonna stay till the end of the year, that's what I keep telling myself, but every Sunday night my stomach's in knots, and I don't think that's how you should feel about a job you like.
I continue to tell myself that I will remain until the end of the year, but every Sunday evening I feel a knot in my stomach, and I do not believe one should feel that way about a job one enjoys.

sentences.note: **knot in my stomach** 는 긴장되거나 걱정돼서 속이 조여드는 느낌이에요. **I keep telling myself** 는 스스로에게 계속 다짐한다는 말이에요.

sentences.ko: 내 폰이 배터리 30퍼센트쯤에서 자꾸 꺼져. 통화하다가 그냥 툭 꺼지고, 다시 충전기 꽂으면 또 30퍼센트래. 이제 뭘 믿어야 할지도 모르겠어.
sentences.text: My phone keeps dying at like thirty percent. It just shuts off in the middle of a call, and then when I plug it back in it says thirty percent again, so I don't even know what to believe anymore.

alts.text: It hits thirty percent and boom, my phone's dead. Happens all the time, right in the middle of calls, and when I plug it back in it says thirty again, so I dunno what to believe anymore.

My phone repeatedly shuts down at approximately thirty percent. It turns off in the middle of a call, and when I charge it again it displays thirty percent once more, so I no longer know what to believe.

sentences.note: **keeps dying** 은 배터리가 자꾸 나간다는 뜻으로, 기계가 꺼질 때 die 를 흔히 써요. **at like thirty percent** 의 like 는 대략, 한 이런 느낌이에요.

reviewed: 1번 note 의 **cram** 은 문장에 그 모양 그대로 나오지 않아 실제로 나오는 **cramming** 으로 바꿨습니다.
4번 note 의 **a knot in my stomach** 는 문장에 a 가 아니라 this 로 나와서, 실제로 나오는 **knot in my stomach** 로 바꿨습니다.
4번 한국어의 속이 꽉 막힌 것처럼 답답해 는 체한 느낌으로 읽힙니다. knot 은 긴장해서 속이 조이는 느낌이라 속이 조여드는 것 같아 로 고쳤습니다.
4번 한국어 끝 문장이 단정하는 말투(안 되는 거잖아)라 영어의 I don't think(~아닌 것 같아)와 어긋나서 짐작하는 말투로 맞췄습니다.
